newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Alliance wants influence to reflect vote.
newsitem.headline: NZ Alliance wants influence to reflect vote.

text.p: Alliance Party leader Jim Anderton said on Wednesday he expected the policies of any government supported by his party to reflect its 10 percent vote in Saturday's election.

Releasing a position paper on the party's conditions for supporting a Labour-New Zealand First government Anderton told a news conference: "We put up our solutions. These solutions got 10 percent of the vote and we acknowledge that."

In an apparently conciliatory move, Anderton said the Alliance was willing to negotiate on some specific policies. He said the Alliance would not join a coalition but was prepared to support a minority government with a programme that made progress towards the Alliance's objectives.

"While the Alliance would not join a coalition government, we are prepared to support a minority government with a programme which makes substantial progress towards our policy objectives," Anderton said.
Co-Deputy Leader Sandra Lee said the paper was "an invitation to engage our support".
Anderton said the Alliance was looking for a written agreement but with an opt-out clause.
Asked in what circumstances he could not support a Labour-NZ First government, Anderton said: "When the policies are against the interests of the people we support absolutely."
Anderton said he expected the government to lose many votes in parliament but it was no reason to force an election.
Only if the government made it an issue of confidence would it cause an election, and such a move would be punished by voters.

Anderton said if a government was not formed by the time parliament is due to convene on December 13 then it indicated a lack of goodwill on the part of those involved. That would be an abdication of responsibility, he said.
